title: Question tags
note: Positive sentence -> negative tag and the reverse; the tag repeats the auxiliary. Czech has one invariant tag (ze jo? / vid? / ze ne?) so students produce *You are coming, no? and *You like it, yes?. Where the sentence has no auxiliary, the tag supplies do/does/did. Thickened 10 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop): 15 new, deliberately weighted toward NEGATIVE sentence + POSITIVE tag (You don't drink tea, do you?), which the stub had only three of and which is the harder direction out of Czech `ze ne?`. Auxiliaries now cover be, do/does/did, have/has, can, will, should and `I am ... am I?`. Rules applied this pass: F3 the subject contraction moved out of `en` into accepts (You're -> You are), which is also where A8 wants it; A8 expansions added wherever the negative sits in the MAIN clause. KNOWN LINT FALSE POSITIVE: A8 asks every NEGATIVE TAG for an expansion that does not exist - the twin of `aren't you?` is `are you not?`, not *are not you?*, which is the exact string the check looks for. Nine items carry that flag and must not be `fixed`: a wrong string in accepts marks a wrong answer right. Same lint gap as the had-to case on b1_past_modals; queued in DECISIONS.md.

cards.title: Question tags
points: Czech uses one little tag for everything. English changes it to match the sentence.

cards.title: The tag copies the auxiliary
points: Find the auxiliary in the sentence and reuse it.

cards.title: When there is no auxiliary
points: The tag brings in **do /** does / did, just as a question would.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: The tag flips the sentence: positive to negative, negative to positive.

accepts: You are coming, aren't you?
You're coming, aren't you?
items.wrong: You are coming, no?
items.explanation: Positive sentence with **are**, so a negative tag with the same verb: aren't you.
items.explanation_cz: Kladná věta s **are**, takže záporný dovětek se stejným slovesem: aren't you.

accepts: She doesn't drive, does she?
She does not drive, does she?
items.wrong: She doesn't drive, doesn't she?
items.explanation: Negative sentence, so the tag is positive: **does she**.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná věta, takže dovětek je kladný: **does she**.

accepts: They went home, didn't they?
items.explanation: Past simple with no auxiliary, so the tag supplies **did**: didn't they.
items.explanation_cz: Minulý čas bez pomocného slovesa, takže dovětek dodá **did**: didn't they.
items.wrong: They went home, didn't they went?

accepts: You like coffee, don't you?
items.wrong: You like coffee, yes?
items.explanation: Present simple with **you**, so the tag is **don't you**.
items.explanation_cz: Přítomný prostý s **you**, takže dovětek je **don't you**.

accepts: He works here, doesn't he?
items.explanation: Third person present simple, so **doesn't he**.
items.explanation_cz: Třetí osoba přítomného prostého, takže **doesn't he**.
items.wrong: He works here, don't he?

items.en: She has left already, hasn't she?
accepts: She has left already, hasn't she?
She's left already, hasn't she?
items.explanation: The auxiliary is **has**, so the tag reuses it: hasn't she.
items.explanation_cz: Pomocné sloveso je **has**, takže ho dovětek zopakuje: hasn't she.
items.wrong: She has left already, isn't she?

accepts: They can swim, can't they?
items.explanation: **can** is the auxiliary, so the negative tag is can't they.
items.explanation_cz: **can** je pomocné sloveso, takže záporný dovětek je can't they.
items.wrong: They can swim, don't they?

items.en: It isn't very expensive, is it?
items.cz: Není to moc drahé, že ne?
accepts: It isn't very expensive, is it?
It is not very expensive, is it?
items.wrong: It isn't very expensive, isn't it?
items.explanation: Negative sentence takes a positive tag: **is it**.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná věta má kladný dovětek: **is it**.

items.en: You didn't call her, did you?
accepts: You didn't call her, did you?
You did not call her, did you?
items.explanation: Negative past, so a positive tag with **did**.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná minulost, takže kladný dovětek s **did**.
items.wrong: You didn't call her, didn't you?

accepts: We are late, aren't we?
We're late, aren't we?
items.explanation: **we're** is we are, so the tag is aren't we.
items.explanation_cz: **we're** je we are, takže dovětek je aren't we.
items.wrong: We are late, no?

items.en: You don't drink tea, do you?
accepts: You don't drink tea, do you?
You do not drink tea, do you?
items.wrong: You don't drink tea, don't you?
items.explanation: The sentence is negative, so the tag is **positive**: do you? Two negatives is the commonest slip.
items.explanation_cz: Věta je záporná, takže dovětek je **kladný**: do you? Dva zápory jsou nejčastější chyba.

accepts: She isn't coming, is she?
She is not coming, is she?
items.wrong: She isn't coming, isn't she?
items.explanation: Negative sentence → **positive** tag, and it copies the same auxiliary: **is**.
items.explanation_cz: Záporná věta → **kladný** dovětek a kopíruje stejné pomocné sloveso: **is**.

accepts: They can't swim, can they?
They cannot swim, can they?
items.wrong: They can't swim, don't they?
items.explanation: The auxiliary is **can**, so the tag is can they? — never do they.
items.explanation_cz: Pomocné sloveso je **can**, takže dovětek je can they? — nikdy do they.

items.en: He didn't tell you, did he?
accepts: He didn't tell you, did he?
He did not tell you, did he?
items.wrong: He didn't tell you, didn't he?
items.explanation: Past simple negative → **did he?**. The tag flips to positive.
items.explanation_cz: Zápor v minulém čase → **did he?**. Dovětek se překlopí do kladu.

items.en: The film wasn't very good, was it?
items.cz: Ten film nebyl moc dobrý, že ne?
accepts: The film wasn't very good, was it?
The film was not very good, was it?
items.wrong: The film wasn't very good, wasn't it?
items.explanation: **the film** is *it* in the tag, and the negative sentence takes the positive **was it?**
items.explanation_cz: **the film** je v dovětku *it* a záporná věta má kladné **was it?**

items.en: We haven't met before, have we?
items.cz: Ještě jsme se nepotkali, že ne?
accepts: We haven't met before, have we?
We have not met before, have we?
items.wrong: We haven't met before, haven't we?
items.explanation: The auxiliary is **have**, so the tag is have we?
items.explanation_cz: Pomocné sloveso je **have**, takže dovětek je have we?

items.en: Your brother doesn't live here, does he?
items.cz: Tvůj brácha tady nebydlí, že ne?
accepts: Your brother doesn't live here, does he?
Your brother does not live here, does he?
items.wrong: Your brother doesn't live here, doesn't he?
items.explanation: **your brother** becomes *he*, and third person negative takes **does he?**
items.explanation_cz: **your brother** se změní na *he* a zápor ve třetí osobě má **does he?**

items.en: You weren't at home, were you?
accepts: You weren't at home, were you?
You were not at home, were you?
items.wrong: You weren't at home, weren't you?
items.explanation: **you** takes were, so the positive tag is **were you?**
items.explanation_cz: **you** má were, takže kladný dovětek je **were you?**

accepts: She hasn't finished, has she?
She has not finished, has she?
items.wrong: She hasn't finished, hasn't she?
items.explanation: Copy the auxiliary **has** and flip it to positive: has she?
items.explanation_cz: Zkopíruj pomocné sloveso **has** a překlop ho do kladu: has she?

accepts: They aren't ready, are they?
They are not ready, are they?
items.wrong: They aren't ready, aren't they?
items.explanation: Negative **aren't** → positive **are they?**
items.explanation_cz: Zápor **aren't** → klad **are they?**

accepts: You won't forget, will you?
You will not forget, will you?
items.wrong: You won't forget, won't you?
items.explanation: **won't** is will + not, so the positive tag is **will you?**
items.explanation_cz: **won't** je will + not, takže kladný dovětek je **will you?**

items.en: I am not late, am I?
accepts: I am not late, am I?
I'm not late, am I?
items.wrong: I am not late, do I?
items.explanation: With **I am** the positive tag is **am I?** — the auxiliary is copied, not replaced.
items.explanation_cz: U **I am** je kladný dovětek **am I?** — pomocné sloveso se kopíruje, nenahrazuje.

accepts: We shouldn't wait, should we?
We should not wait, should we?
items.wrong: We shouldn't wait, shouldn't we?
items.explanation: Any auxiliary works the same way: **shouldn't** → should we?
items.explanation_cz: Každé pomocné sloveso funguje stejně: **shouldn't** → should we?

items.en: She lives in Prague, doesn't she?
accepts: She lives in Prague, doesn't she?
items.wrong: She lives in Prague, isn't she?
items.explanation: No auxiliary in the sentence, so the tag brings in **does** — and she is third person.
items.explanation_cz: Ve větě není pomocné sloveso, takže dovětek přinese **does** — a ona je třetí osoba.

items.en: They will be here soon, won't they?
accepts: They will be here soon, won't they?
They'll be here soon, won't they?
items.wrong: They will be here soon, will they?
items.explanation: Positive sentence → **negative** tag: won't they?
items.explanation_cz: Kladná věta → **záporný** dovětek: won't they?
